properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Digest/`==` comparisons in py-evm chain validation, DB integrity checks, fork header/block validation and test assertions. All 62 sites compare public blockchain values (header hashes, trie roots, tx/receipt/uncle roots, genesis constants) — no secret or MAC operand exists anywhere in this codebase, so the timing-leak premise of the rule does not apply. Recorded as a posture note; a future security-sensitive comparison (e.g. of private material) would warrant constant-time comparison.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Keccak-256/512 (original Keccak padding, pre-FIPS-202) is Ethereum's core protocol hash, supplied by the eth_hash library (pycryptodome/pysha3 backend). Protocol-mandated by the Ethereum spec — NOT changeable in this repo without a network-wide consensus fork; observable here, replaceable only by the protocol. Quantum impact limited to Grover's square-root speedup (hashes are not Shor-broken), hence the A- rating.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Vendored pure-Python BLAKE2b F-compression function (EIP-152) exposed as precompile 0x09 from Istanbul onward; optional C-accelerated blake2b-py>=0.2.0 backend declared in setup.py:47 (eth-extra). Protocol-mandated by EIP-152; the EVM exposes the raw compression call with caller-supplied parameters rather than keyed BLAKE2b hashing, so no key material exists here. BLAKE2 itself is Grover-only quantum-affected.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Two protocol-mandated SHA-256 uses in py-evm: (1) the 0x02 SHA-256 precompile (EIP-101) exposing SHA-256 hashing to EVM contracts, and (2) kzg_to_versioned_hash() deriving blob versioned-hash from KZG commitments per EIP-4844 (VERSIONED_HASH_VERSION_KZG byte + sha256(commitment)[1:]). Both fixed by the Ethereum protocol spec; hash primitive, Grover-only quantum impact.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Test factory generating secp256k1 private keys: secrets.randbits(256) → 32-byte PrivateKey for test fixtures. Test-only key material generation using a correct CSPRNG (secrets module, os.urandom-backed). The secp256k1 ECDSA those keys feed is protocol-locked and reported separately; this object records the randomness source.
